_readme: THE MODEL REGISTRY. Read by fpms-model-verify, and by anything that wants
to know what a .rknn on this rover is supposed to be BEFORE it trusts the
numbers coming out of it.
JSON has no comments, so the prose lives in _readme and in the per-model
"notes" arrays. Keys beginning with an underscore are documentation and are
ignored by every consumer.
WHY A SHA256 IS null HERE AND NOT A PLAUSIBLE-LOOKING STRING
yolo26n-rk3588.rknn IS NOT IN THE GIT REPOSITORY. It exists on exactly one
SD card, in one Pi, and has never been hashed by anybody. We therefore do
not have its sha256, and a fabricated one is strictly worse than none: a
wrong hash makes fpms-model-verify FAIL on the one genuinely correct file
the project owns, and the obvious way an operator 'fixes' that is to stop
checking hashes at all.
So the missing value is VISIBLY missing. sha256 is null, sha256_status says
why, and verified is false. Same precedent as calibration.json: a missing
profile changes nothing, a guessed one is silent and total.
null is not a shrug. It is a declared, checkable state - fpms-model-verify
reports UNVERIFIED for it, exits non-zero, and prints the observed hash so a
human can put it here with `fpms-model-verify --register` on the day the
file is first seen on hardware.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY VERIFIED IN THIS FILE
Shapes, names, class count and the end2end=false requirement were read off
the source ONNX and are recorded in fpms_yolo26_npu.py's header, which was
written from an op histogram of that graph. Those are evidence.
The hash, the converter version and the runtime this was built against are
UNKNOWN, and are marked UNKNOWN rather than filled in.

yolo26n.description: YOLO26-nano, COCO-80, converted for RK3588 NPU. The detector the rover actually runs.
_file_note: Hardcoded as MODEL in fpms_yolo26_npu.py. If you move the model you must
change both, or the decode module and this registry will describe
different files and nothing will say so.
yolo26n.sha256_status: UNKNOWN - the file has never been in git and has never been hashed. Not fabricated. See _readme.
_verified_note: verified:true means: a named human ran fpms-model-verify on real RK3588S
hardware, the sha256 below matched the file on disk, the model loaded
under RKNNLite, init_runtime() returned 0, and the OBSERVED output shape
was [1,84,8400]. Nothing less sets this flag. In particular a hash
recorded with --register while the NPU was unavailable leaves this false
and sets sha256_status to RECORDED_UNVERIFIED - we know WHICH file it is,
we still do not know that it works.

input.name: images
input.evidence: read off models/yolo26n.onnx; recorded in fpms_yolo26_npu.py header
_feed_note: The GRAPH is NCHW, but the agent hands rknn.inference() an NHWC uint8
np.expand_dims(img,0), i.e. [1,640,640,3] uint8 RGB. The RKNN runtime
does the transpose. fpms-model-verify feeds the same NHWC uint8 form
on purpose - a probe that fed NCHW float would be testing a path the
Preprocessing is a STRETCH resize, not a letterbox, so box rescaling is
an independent per-axis ratio with no padding term. If preprocessing
ever becomes a letterbox, fpms_yolo26_npu.decode needs padding
compensation added and this note is the warning that it does.

output.name: output0
_shape_note: THIS IS THE CHECK THAT MATTERS MOST. A wrong-shaped model does not
raise; it produces garbage boxes that look exactly like detections.
RKNN is not consistent about whether it returns [1,84,8400] or a
channel-last [1,8400,84], and may drop the batch axis - fpms_yolo26_npu
._as_anchor_major() locates the 84 axis rather than trusting one
layout. fpms-model-verify accepts any permutation whose non-unit axes
are {84, 8400} and records which one it actually saw.

channels.box_form: xywh CENTRE, already multiplied by the per-anchor stride constant, i.e. in 640x640 input-pixel units
channels.class_form: ALREADY SIGMOIDED - these are probabilities in [0,1]. DO NOT SIGMOID AGAIN.

postprocess_on_cpu: confidence threshold, then a light per-class NMS, in fpms_yolo26_npu.decode.
'NMS-free' describes how YOLO26 was TRAINED. With end2end=false the
exported head still emits all 8400 anchors and the CPU still thresholds.

labels.status: NO LABEL FILE EXISTS ON THIS ROVER.
_note: The 80 COCO names are a COCO_NAMES list compiled into
fpms_rover_agent.py. There is no labels.txt, no coco.names, and nothing
in the image writes one. Naming a file here that does not exist would
be the same fabrication as inventing a hash.
There IS an optional operator override: ${FPMS_YOLO_DIR}/custom_labels.json,
a {"<class_id>": "display name"} map the agent loads inside a bare
try/except - a malformed or absent file is silently ignored and the
COCO names are used. It renames what is drawn; it does NOT change what
the model detects, and it is not a source of truth for class ids.
FIRE IS NOT A COCO CLASS. Fire detection in this rover is a colour
heuristic in the agent, not a model output. Do not read a fire alert as
evidence that the NPU is working.

_end2end_note: MANDATORY, and the single most dangerous knob in the conversion.
Ultralytics' own RKNN documentation reports that end2end=True emits
[1,300,6] and that its top-k op SEGFAULTS ON THE NPU.
A segfault on load is a spectacularly bad failure mode: the agent wraps
the whole NPU block in one try/except, but a SIGSEGV is not an
exception - the process dies, systemd restarts it, and it dies again.
Catching this by SHAPE, before anything runs it, is the entire point of
